author: Ross, Malcolm
title: Areal phonological features in north central New Ireland
notes: Consulted directly on 26 November 2026 (PDF of the volume in Downloads; tables read from page images). A 'phonological alliance' of the Papuan language Kuot with the Oceanic languages Lamasong and Madak (and, more weakly, Nalik and Kara), ascribed to shift by earlier Kuot speakers. §2: the languages, of three local groups descended from a Proto-New Ireland dialect network (Ross 1988: 261-262, 280, 291-292): Lavongai/Nalik, Tabar (Notsi) and Madak (Lamasong, Madak, Barok). §3.1: the consonant systems of PNI (1), PLN with its daughters (2), PNI > Patpatar and PMAD > Barok, Madak, Lamasong (3), PMAD (5), Kuot (6), p. 556-557. §3.2: the shared rules l > n / _# (7) and voiceless stop > voiced fricative between vowels (11), the Nalik and Kara variant (30). Data from the author's consultants (n. 2).
